{{Recipe}}

'''Camotes enmielados''', also known as '''camotes con pilocilo''', or '''camotes enmielados al horno''', '''camotes con piloncilo al horno''', is a baked, or stovetop, dessert-style Mexican yam/sweet potato dish. It is traditionally a home-cooked food, not typical restaurant fare. The finished product should have a strong caramel flavor, with a typical hint of bitterness from the molasses component of the sugar used. The sauce should be syrupy and very dark in color. The cinnamon flavor should be an accent, and not dominating.

==Ingredients==
*1 large [[Cookbook:Yam|yam]] or [[Cookbook:Sweet Potato|sweet potato]], optionally peeled
*1 large piloncilo cone (unrefined Mexican [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]])
*4 sticks [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
*½ water

== Procedure ==

# Place whole or thickly-sliced yams in a large [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|baking dish]].
# Place piloncilo cone atop the yams, then add water and cinnamon.
# Cover dish, and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] for about 60 minutes, [[Cookbook:Basting|basting]] the yams with the now sweetened cooking liquid as needed.

== Notes, tips, and variation ==

* Any dark, unrefined sugar may be reasonably substituted for the piloncilo, including [[Cookbook:Turbinado Sugar|turbinado sugar]], [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]], brown sugar with added molasses, muscovado, and even [[Cookbook:Jaggery|jaggery]].

[[File:Vendedor de camotes - Ciudad de México..jpg|thumb|Street vendor applying sweetened condensed milk to Camotes, Mexico City]]

==Further reading==
*''Latin American Street Food: The Best Flavors of Markets, Beaches, and Roadside Stands from Mexico to Argentina'', Sandra A. Gutierrez. The University of North Carolina Press (2013), ISBN: 978-1469608709
